brief.headline: Move to 30-day credit to free up ₹8.73 L of our cash and cut their price by 6.5% to match our best supplier

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the price Sayaji Industries gives us today
priceAsk.basis: Right now we pay them ₹70.80/KG while Sayaji charges ₹66.48/KG for the same Dextrose Anhydrous IP — that's a 6.5% gap. The open market asking price for this item sits at ₹66–73/KG typical, so ₹66.48 is fair and proven. We should pay one price across all suppliers.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Stop paying 100% in advance; move to normal 30-day credit after delivery
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's currently locked in advance payments

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit is big — ₹1555.82 Cr in sales — but keeps only 2.9% as profit, so margins are paper-thin. We're tiny to them: our ₹1.06 Cr is just 0.07% of everything they sell, which means we have almost no pull on our own. They are growing fast (29.7% per year), so they want volume. The play is to bundle: commit more kilos or a longer contract in exchange for the price cut and better payment terms, and quietly line up Gulshan or Sanstar as a second source so we're not stuck.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹70.80/KG while our best supplier charges ₹66.48/KG — a 6.5% gap
We pay 100% upfront, locking up ₹8.73 L of our cash that 30-day terms would free
Our spend is only 0.07% of their ₹1555.82 Cr revenue — we're a very small customer
They keep just 2.9% profit, so every rupee matters to them
Their sales are growing 29.7% per year — they need volume
Market asking price for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹66–73/KG typical, so ₹66.48 is fair

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch and dextrose maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health score B (62/100) — a strong, established drop-in alternate to Sayaji and Sukhjit

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist with growing dextrose capacity, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C (53/100) — good second-source option

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller making Dextrose Anhydrous IV-fluid grade (exact form match), ₹365.39 Cr revenue — confirm IP monograph certificate of analysis before switching

risks: We're 0.07% of their business, so they can easily walk away — don't push hard without a volume sweetener or a signed backup
Their profit is only 2.9%, so a big price cut with no volume increase might make them drop us or cut corners on quality
We pay 100% advance today, which is terrible for us but great for them — they may resist credit terms more than price
They're growing fast (29.7%/year) and may have other customers willing to pay more — time the ask when we can commit a longer contract or bigger order
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to grow our dextrose volume with you, but to do that we need two things: a price that matches what Sayaji gives us at ₹66.48/KG, and normal 30-day credit instead of paying everything up front.
